title: Parabolic-trough receiver (HCE) - 1D radial energy balance of the Forristal/NREL model (glass envelope, vacuum annulus, wind, sky radiation)
description: Per cell: optical chain eta_opt = eps1*...*eps6*rho_cl*cos(theta) (incidence-angle modifier = cos theta), absorbed flux on glass (Alpha_g) and on the tube (Alpha_t*Tau_g), radial conduction through tube and glass walls (half-thickness resistances), annulus heat transfer by free-molecular conduction (mean free path from T, vacuum pressure and molecular diameter, k_st, interaction coefficient) plus radiation tube-glass (Eps_t(T) = 0.062 + 2e-7*(T-273.15)^2, Eps_g = 0.89), external forced convection (Re-dependent C, m, n constants), radiation to the sky (T_sky = T_amb - 8). Outputs: heat loss per reflector area, thermal and total efficiency, absorbed power. Inputs: DNI, T_amb, wind speed, incidence angle and the tube-wall temperature given by the heat-transfer fluid.
fluids: none (air and annulus-gas constants; heat-transfer fluid enters through the tube-wall temperature)
authors: Adriano Desideri; Sylvain Quoilin; model of R. Forristal (NREL, 2003)
notes: difficulty=medium; steady in essence: the only dynamic terms are rho*Cp*A*der(T_g) and der(T_t) (thermal mass of glass and tube), so der = 0 gives the steady radial balance, about ten equations per cell with T^4 radiation, no property calls. Keep it a single cell (receiver at a given tube temperature, level 2) and add a DUPLICATE chain with the fluid for the collector (level 3). Re-dependent IFs for C and m are non-smooth: fix the regime. Spotted in the source: radiation term uses Eps_t[N] (last cell) instead of Eps_t[i]; optical parameters (eps1..eps6, rho_cl) are inputs, the parent SolarField_Forristal comments give eta_opt = 0.7263. The file cites NREL/TP-550-34169 (R. Forristal 2003; the report title says the model was implemented in EES, so a translation back to EES is natural) and comments mention validation against Sandia SEGS LS-2 data. reference results: none stored (the Modelica tests are time-series drivers without asserted values; OpenModelica/Dymola not available); verify against the NREL report (heat loss and efficiency of the LS-2 receiver vs tube temperature) and the NREL Schott PTR70 heat-loss test (Burkholder and Kutscher 2009), plus the energy balance closure. gap: renewables/solar_thermal is empty in the library and the thermo_models collection has no collector model.

title: Parabolic-trough receiver and collector heat-loss correlations - NREL Schott PTR70 test fits (vacuum, lost vacuum, hydrogen), Sopogy MicroCSP, Soltigua PTMx datasheet efficiency
description: Heat loss per metre of absorber HL = A0 + A1*(T-T_amb) + A2*T^2 + A3*T^3 + A4*DNI*IAM*T^2 + sqrt(v_wind)*(A5 + A6*(T-T_amb)) [W/m, T in degC] with coefficient records for the Schott PTR70 receiver (vacuum record: 4.05, 0.247, -1.46e-3, 5.65e-6, 7.62e-8, -1.7, 0.0125), PTR70 with lost vacuum, PTR70 with hydrogen and the Sopogy MicroCSP receiver; optical efficiency rho_cl*eps6*cos(theta)*Alpha_t*tau_g; thermal efficiency 1 - loss/absorbed flux. Soltigua PTMx (18, 24, 30, 36, 100): eta = K_l(theta)*0.747 - 0.64*(T-T_amb)/DNI with a cubic longitudinal incidence-angle modifier and a net aperture area per model.
fluids: none (heat-transfer fluid enters through the receiver temperature)
authors: Adriano Desideri; Sylvain Quoilin; correlations of F. Burkholder and C. Kutscher (NREL 2009), Soltigua and Sopogy datasheets
notes: difficulty=easy; one explicit FUNCTION per absorber type plus coefficient sets (the records become arguments or a lookup of coefficient arrays). Do it together with LTP-050 and LTP-020 (Dickes-Lemort-Quoilin 10-coefficient form for Soponova) so that the function names, the unit convention and the README are shared, and cross-check against THC-001. Data to check before use: (i) the SopoNova record coefficients (11.8, 1.35, 7.5e-4, 4.07e-6, 5.85e-8, -4.48, 0.285) are identical to the PTR70 Hydrogen record, probably a copy; (ii) Soltigua BaseGeometry has A_3 = -2-6.94444444E-07 (looks like a typo for -6.94444444E-07); (iii) AbsSoltigua appears to count the 0.64 W/(m2 K) loss twice (inside the efficiency and again as Phi_amb); reference results: the NREL PTR70 heat-loss test report (measured data and the fit, F. Burkholder and C. Kutscher, May 2009) and the Soltigua PTMx datasheets REV03-04/2013 and REV09-08/2013 cited in the file; none stored in the repository. gap: second collector family beside LTP-020/LTP-050.

title: ORC machines from empirical maps - volumetric expander (hermetic scroll, open-drive scroll, single screw) isentropic efficiency and filling factor, centrifugal pump curves and test-rig pressure-drop fits
description: Expander: V_dot_su = FF*V_s*N, h_ex = h_su - eps_s*(h_su - h_ex_s), W_dot = M_dot*(h_su - h_ex), with eps_s and FF taken from empirical maps: hermetic scroll (polynomials in log(rho_su) and log(p_su/p_ex), clamps eps_s <= 0.65 and 1 <= FF <= 1.2), open-drive scroll (polynomials in N_rot, rho_su, log(p_su/p_ex), clamps eps_s <= 0.79 and 0.576 <= FF <= 1.592), generic single screw expander (efficiency curve D*sin(C*atan(...)) of the pressure ratio shifted by speed and inlet pressure, mass flow polynomial in pressure and speed). Pump: M_dot from the frequency, eta_in from f_pp and p_ex/p_su (ORCnext rig) or from the flow fraction (0.931 - 0.108*log10(X) - ..., SQ thesis), h_ex = h_su + dp/(eta*rho_su). Lines of the rig: dp = k1*M_dot + k2*M_dot^2.
fluids: R245fa (test rig); any CoolProp fluid for the demo
authors: Adriano Desideri; Sylvain Quoilin; Jorrit Wronski (git history of the correlation files)
notes: difficulty=easy; explicit polynomials, one FUNCTION per map, the machine models are 6-8 equations each; the demo can be a small closed ORC (pump, specified evaporator and condenser, expander) that does not exist in steady form in ThermoCycle. Maps are machine-specific and their validity ranges are not documented: outside the calibration range the polynomials leave the physical range (hermetic scroll eps_s = -1.6 before the clamp at rho_su = 10 kg/m3 and p ratio 2, checked with Python), so keep the clamps (non-smooth min/max, replace by smooth versions or range checks). Modelica ExpTypes has no ORCnext type although the step_by_step examples use it (stale examples): translate the function files, not the examples. Complements CSL-0037 (Lemort semi-empirical expander) and CSL-0038 (polynomial maps in a CO2 ORC): same map approach for volumetric expanders and pump curves. reference results: none stored; verify by an independent Python evaluation of the polynomials with CoolProp 8.0.0 states and physical sanity; the publications listed in the ThermoCycle docs (Quoilin PhD thesis 2011, Desideri et al. 2013 screw expander WHR ORC) are the probable sources of the fits, the maintainer can confirm.

title: Flow-boiling and nucleate-boiling heat-transfer coefficients - Shah 1982 chart correlation, Gungor-Winterton 1987, Cooper 1984 (smooth regime transitions)
description: Shah 1982 saturated boiling in a tube (convection number Co, boiling number Bo, liquid Froude number Fr_l, parameter N, enhancement factor psi from the convective and nucleate-boiling branches for N > 1, 0.1 < N <= 1 and N <= 0.1, vertical or horizontal switch) times the liquid-only Dittus-Boelter coefficient; Gungor-Winterton 1987 simplified form h = h_l*(1 + 3000*Bo^0.86 + 1.12*(x/(1-x))^0.75*(rho_l/rho_v)^0.41)*Fr term; Cooper 1984 pool boiling h = C*55*p_r^(0.12-0.2*log10(R_p))*(-log10(p_r))^-0.55*M^-0.5*q^0.67 (C = enhancement for plate exchangers). Regime switches are blended with a smooth transition function.
fluids: any (CoolProp); liquid and vapour saturation properties
authors: Jorrit Wronski (git history); Adriano Desideri; Sylvain Quoilin
notes: difficulty=easy-medium; explicit and the equations are numbered in the Modelica source (Eq. 1 to 14 for Shah). Overlap: the LTP-034 function library has Gungor-Winterton, Steiner-Taborek and Choi flow boiling (Cooper appears inside the Choi function and in LTP-041) but not Shah 1982, which exists in LaboThapPy only as a simplified inline block of the legacy script of LTP-054 (skip); the documented, numbered ThermoCycle version is therefore the new content. Card it after LTP-034/LTP-035, reuse their liquid-only coefficient and keep the function names unique across the library. CoolSolve solves implicit sets, so keep the smooth blends (or max/min) between the regimes. reference results: none stored (Test_HeatTransferTester is a driver without asserted values; its plate geometry is a_hat = 1.2 mm, phi = 65 deg, Lambda = 7.5 mm, B_p = 40 mm); verify by an independent Python implementation with CoolProp 8.0.0 properties and against the published formulas and test data of Shah (ASHRAE Trans. 88, 1982) and Gungor and Winterton (Chem. Eng. Res. Des. 65, 1987), which are not in the repository.

title: In-cylinder heat-transfer correlations for reciprocating engines and compressors - Annand 1963, Woschni 1967, Adair 1972, Destoop 1986, Irimescu 2013, Kornhauser 1994 (gas spring)
description: Nu = a*Re^b*Pr^c with characteristic length and velocity per correlation, h = Nu*lambda/L: Annand (a = 0.575, b = 0.7, bore, mean piston speed), Woschni (a = 0.035, b = 0.8, velocity 2.28*mean piston speed, compression phase only), Adair (a = 0.053, b = 0.8, c = 0.6, swirl velocity from the crank angle and equivalent diameter 6*V/A, smooth switch between the two swirl branches), Destoop (a = 0.6, b = 0.8, c = 0.6), Irimescu (Gnielinski pipe equation with viscosity ratio, current piston speed) and Kornhauser gas-spring Nu = 0.56*Pe^0.69 with Pe from the angular speed and the hydraulic diameter 4*V/A; wall area = piston area + bore*pi*clearance.
fluids: any gas (needs viscosity, conductivity, Prandtl number, density)
notes: difficulty=easy; explicit, scalar functions of (rho, eta, lambda, cp or Pr, bore, stroke, crank angle, mean and current piston speed). Simplified versions: Woschni without the combustion term, Annand without radiation, motored conditions; the documentation of Destoop1986 cites Annand 1963 (copy-paste, check the reference). Value: CSL-0024 (single-cylinder Weibe model, constant U_w = 500 W/(m2 K)) and the engine candidates of thermo_models have no in-cylinder correlation; the correlations are algebraic although the machine models that use them are dynamic (crank angle). Provenance: the reciprocating package carries a DTU copyright (2011-2013, J. Wronski) and a Modelica License 2 notice while the repository license is MIT: credit J. Wronski as for any translated model and confirm with him. reference results: none stored; verify against the original papers and an independent Python evaluation with CoolProp air properties.

title: EN12900 polynomial compressors - 10-coefficient maps of five Copeland ZH scroll compressors (R134a) and one ZRD digital scroll (R407c)
description: Mass flow and electrical power as cubic bivariate polynomials of the evaporation and condensing temperatures (degF inputs, lbm/h output with the factor 125.9979e-6), swept volumes 34.03 to 98.04 cm3; the model recovers the isentropic and volumetric efficiencies from the polynomial mass flow, power and swept volume.
notes: difficulty=easy; same polynomial form as TSP-006 (TESPy EN12900) and as the Copeland catalogue models TM-0288/TM-0289: not a card by itself, add the six coefficient sets to the TSP-006 card as data or variants (unit conversion degF and lbm/h needed). Coefficients are Copeland catalogue data (check redistribution). reference results: none stored.

title: Heat-transfer-fluid property tables - Mobiltherm, Therminol 66, Therminol SP, ethylene glycol, flue gas (density, specific heat, conductivity, viscosity vs temperature)
description: Tabulated incompressible-fluid properties as functions of temperature (0 to 380 degC depending on the fluid; flue gas 150 to 1000 degC as specific volume).
fluids: Mobiltherm; Therminol 66; Therminol SP; ethylene glycol; flue gas
notes: difficulty=easy; data only. CoolProp 8.0.0 already has Therminol 66 (T66), Therminol VP-1 (TVP1), Dow Q and ethylene-glycol solutions; Mobiltherm, Therminol SP and the flue-gas table are not in its incompressible list, so only these are new. Data issues: the Therminol 66 table has cp(20 degC) = 1008.4 J/(kg K), a density value pasted into the heat-capacity table; the flue-gas density column is written 1/1287, 1/1318... under a comment saying kg/m3, which only makes sense as kg/L (units to check). Manufacturer data: check redistribution. Not a card; use as lookup tables only if a solar or ORC model needs these oils.

title: Semi-empirical hermetic scroll compressor (Winandy et al.) and detailed open-drive scroll expander (Lemort/Quoilin) - Modelica versions
description: Six-process semi-empirical models (supply pressure drop, supply heat exchange, isentropic then isochoric compression or expansion, leakage and mixing, exhaust heat exchange, mechanical losses, wall energy balance); compressor parameters identified from the Copeland ZR72KC-TFD catalogue; steady with der(T_wall) = 0 (wall mass and rotor inertia are optional).
notes: difficulty=n/a; discarded: same models as CSL-0007 (Winandy scroll compressor, TM-0481, same ZR72KC-TFD data) and CSL-0037 (Lemort/Quoilin scroll expander, TM-0272), already in the library (not diffed line by line); at most a cross-check or an extra parameter set (r_v_in 2.85, V_s 110 cm3 for the expander). Overlaps LTP-002 and LTP-005.

title: Steam turbine with Stodola cone law, regularised, partial-arc admission and constant isentropic efficiency
description: Mass flow M_dot = partialArc*K*sqrt(p_su*rho_su)*sqrt(1-(1/PR)^2) (regularised), constant isentropic efficiency and mechanical efficiency, K from nominal conditions; the shaft flange adds der(phi).
notes: difficulty=n/a; discarded: covered by TSP-003 (TESPy turbine with Stodola cone law and efficiency characteristic, wave1); only the partial-arc factor differs.

title: Real-fluid isentropic nozzle with subsonic and choked flow (throat state from the speed of sound, fictitious gamma option)
description: Throat state from an isentropic expansion, C_thr = sqrt(2*(h_in - h_thr)), mass flow = rho_thr*C_thr*A, choked flow when C_thr reaches the speed of sound (choked throat pressure found implicitly, or from a fictitious perfect-gas gamma), linear flow law below a minimum pressure drop.
fluids: any (CoolProp); water and R245fa in the tests
notes: difficulty=n/a; discarded: covered by TM-0002 (isentropic nozzle with critical pressure, real-gas gamma) and by the leakage nozzle of CSL-0020/CSL-0007; the real-fluid choking condition by speed of sound is the only difference.

title: Single-phase and plate-exchanger heat-transfer correlations - Martin 2010 (VDI Atlas, with plate friction factor), Gnielinski 2010, Muley-Manglik 1999, Dittus-Boelter 1930, Yan-Lin 1999 evaporation and Yan-Lio-Lin 1999 condensation in plates
description: Explicit Nusselt correlations for pipes (Gnielinski laminar/turbulent blend, Dittus-Boelter) and chevron plate exchangers (Martin with enhancement factor and Hagen-number friction factor, Muley-Manglik laminar/turbulent blend), and the R134a plate-exchanger boiling and condensation correlations of Yan et al. using an equivalent mass flux.
authors: Jorrit Wronski (git history); Adriano Desideri; Sylvain Quoilin
notes: difficulty=n/a; discarded: covered by LTP-034 (Gnielinski, Dittus-Boelter), LTP-035 (Martin, Muley-Manglik, Yan boiling and plate HTC) and TM-0319 (Martin plate model); ThermoCycle brings no extra correlation here, use these files only to cross-check the translations (same published correlations, ULiege/DTU implementations).

title: Trivial steady components - valves with incompressible flow, lumped static + linear + quadratic pressure drop, constant-efficiency pump and compressor, semi-isothermal e-NTU exchanger, constant-cp air cells (12 files)
description: Orifice law Mdot = A*sqrt(2*rho*dp) with opening, three-term pressure drop dp = h*rho*g + k*Mdot/rho + Mdot^2/(2*rho*A^2), isenthalpic valves, constant isentropic and volumetric efficiency machines, e-NTU exchanger with eps = 1 - exp(-NTU) against an isothermal wall, constant-specific-heat air cell without dynamics.
notes: difficulty=n/a; discarded: textbook blocks already in the library (CSL-0001 compressor, CSL-0002/0026/0027 e-NTU) or in other inventories (TSP-019 valve, TSP-001 and TSP-005 machines, LTP-001/LTP-004/LTP-008/LTP-010 constant-efficiency machines and valve); the semi-isothermal exchanger is the suction/exhaust heat exchange of the Lemort models (CSL-0007).

title: Dynamic finite-volume flow models and heat exchangers: Flow1Dim/Cell1Dim pipes, metal walls, Hx1D family, CrossHX, CrossCondenser, BoilerSystem, MBeva (26 files)
description: Discretised one-dimensional flow cells with dynamic mass and energy balances (enthalpy and pressure states, der(h), der(p), density derivatives, flow-reversal and limiter options), metal-wall thermal mass, and the heat exchangers built from them; the steadystate flags only set der = 0 at initialisation.
notes: difficulty=n/a; discarded: dynamic by construction (der() in the cells or in the metal wall; the heat exchangers and BoilerSystem instantiate Flow1Dim/Cell1Dim/MetalWall); excluded by the maintainer rule on dynamic models. The steady discretised counterparts are in TSP-013, LTP-012 and CSL-0008.

title: Moving-boundary heat-exchanger package (evaporators and condensers: dry, flooded, general, with and without wall, incompressible secondary fluid) (38 files)
description: Dynamic moving-boundary cells (one-phase and two-phase cells with variable lengths and mean void-fraction terms Theta and Gamma), walls, secondary-fluid models and the evaporator and condenser units assembled from them, with records, functions and connectors.
notes: difficulty=n/a; discarded: dynamic (der() in every cell, 17 to 31 per cell file) and excluded by the maintainer rule; Theta and Gamma are the time-derivative coefficients of the cell mass and energy balances, not a void-fraction correlation. Steady moving-boundary and three-zone models: TSP-014, LTP-016, LTP-013, CSL-0008 and CSL-0014.

title: Dynamic tanks, drums, deaerator and thermocline storage (Tank, ExpansionTank, OpenTank, Tank_pL, Drum_pL, Boiler_drum, Deaerator, ThermoclineStorage, stratified water heater) (10 files)
description: Lumped and nodal storage models with pressure and enthalpy or level states and der() mass and energy balances; stratified water-heater tank with immersed heat exchanger; thermocline with solid filler.
notes: difficulty=n/a; discarded: dynamic (der() or Drum_pL wrappers) and excluded by the maintainer rule; no steady storage sizing model in the library (the closest, TM-0413 and CSL-0009, are the dynamic DHW tank).

title: Dynamic solar fields (Forristal, Schott/Sopogy and Soltigua collectors, compressible and incompressible fluid) (6 files)
description: Collector rows built from Flow1Dim or Flow1DimInc cells coupled to the absorber models; the dynamic heat-transfer fluid and the metal wall are solved with the absorber.
notes: difficulty=n/a; discarded: dynamic (Flow1Dim cells); the steady absorber models they contain are kept as THC-001 and THC-002.

title: Crank-angle reciprocating machine models (slider-crank kinematics, cylinder, valves with timers, closed volume, geometry records, wall segment) (17 files)
description: Dynamic reciprocating expander and compressor models built on Modelica.Fluid vessels and multibody or rotational mechanics, with valve timing and in-cylinder heat transfer models.
notes: difficulty=n/a; discarded: dynamic (crank-angle integration, der() on position, inertia and volume) and excluded by the maintainer rule; the in-cylinder heat-transfer correlations of the same package are kept as THC-005.

title: Example plants and step-by-step cycles: ORC R245fa (10 steps and plant variants), R407c heat pump (10 steps), SQ thesis model with control, chattering example (26 files)
description: Assemblies of the dynamic components (Hx1D, Hx1DConst, tanks, MBeva, pump and expander with ramps on frequency and speed, StopTime 50 to 1669 s).
notes: difficulty=n/a; discarded: all 26 examples assemble dynamic components with time ramps; there is no steady-state cycle example in the repository. Some are stale (step9 uses ExpTypes.ORCNext which the enumeration does not define). Steady ORC and heat pump models already exist (CSL-0019, CSL-0036, CSL-0033, CSL-0068) or are listed (LTP-055, LTP-056, TSP-046).

title: Obsolete superseded models (old Flow1Dim, Hx, solar collector, absorber and detailed expander versions) (27 files)
description: Earlier versions of the flow, heat-exchanger, collector and absorber models and of the hermetic detailed expander, kept for old examples.
notes: difficulty=n/a; discarded: superseded versions: 21 of the 27 files are old dynamic flow, heat-exchanger, collector and plant models, the others are 3 old sources and sinks, the earlier absorber files SolAbs and AbsorberSchott (replaced by the files kept in THC-001 and THC-002) and ExpanderHermeticDetailed (the hermetic variant of the Lemort expander, covered by THC-008).

title: Test harnesses, validation drivers and unit tests (Examples/Test*, MB_HX Tests, reciprocating TestCases and Examples) (131 files)
description: Model drivers with sources, sinks and ramps for components, heat-transfer correlations, fluids, derivatives and numerical methods, evaporator and condenser validation cases; no asserted reference values.
notes: difficulty=n/a; discarded: test harnesses (excluded as infrastructure); none stores reference results or asserts, so they cannot serve as verification data (OpenModelica or Dymola with ExternalMedia would be needed to run them).

title: Infrastructure: package declarations, icons, connectors and converters, media wrappers, enumerations, users guide, partial and base classes, sources, sinks and sensors, control systems, numerical smoothing helpers, correlation wrappers for the dynamic cells (310 files)
description: Modelica package files (95), icons (35), Flange and thermal-port connectors and converters (18), ExternalMedia/CoolProp media wrappers and the Media test package (67 incl. package files), enumerations (8), licence and contacts (2), partial classes (19), boundary conditions and sensors (28), controllers (7), transition_factor, weightingfactor, U_hx, U_sf, RLMTD, Init and start-value helpers (11), HTC wrappers and coupling components (20).
notes: difficulty=n/a; discarded: pure infrastructure with no physical content of its own; RLMTD is the regularised LMTD of Quoilin already listed as TSP-029, transition_factor and weightingfactor are numerical devices for dynamic simulation.
